guidance: Separate permissibility from feasibility. An action's checks say only whether the actor is allowed or positioned to begin it (rules of the game, location, possession). Never check whether the attempt will succeed: do not refuse an action because a resource is too low to finish it. Starting a multi-step activity sets the actor's or object's activity state. Autonomous processes then advance that activity every tick, consume or produce stocks, and switch the activity to a stopped or failed state when a needed stock runs out, or to a finished state when it completes. Every numeric stock needs a process or action for each way it can rise and each way it can fall.
not_modeled: The exact movement and fuel-consumption consequences of actions
The condition that the vehicle stops and fails when it lacks fuel
The restriction that refueling is available only at mile 60
The delivery trip ending after arrival

allowed_only_when: Driving is allowed only while the vehicle is operational and has enough fuel for the next 10-mile movement.
Refueling is allowed only when the vehicle is at mile 60, the gas station is open, and gas-station fuel stock is greater than zero.
The purchased amount must be nonnegative and cannot exceed the vehicle tank's remaining capacity or the gas station's available fuel stock.
The trip succeeds only if the vehicle reaches mile 120 while operational.
may_attempt: Stop at the gas station at mile 60.
Purchase fuel at the gas station.
Purchase enough fuel to fill the vehicle tank or purchase a smaller amount.

assumptions: The vehicle's fuel tank capacity is estimated at 16 gallons, a typical passenger-vehicle capacity.
A quarter tank is interpreted as exactly 25% of capacity, giving an initial fuel level of 4 gallons.
Fuel economy is estimated at 25 miles per gallon, equivalent to a consumption rate of 0.04 gallons per mile.
Fuel consumption is constant and does not vary with speed, terrain, traffic, weather, or driving behavior.
The gas station has an estimated initial fuel stock of 1000 gallons and does not receive resupply during the simulation.
The gas station is open and operational when the driver reaches mile 60.
The vehicle can refuel instantaneously within the tick in which it reaches the gas station.
The driver begins at mile 0 and the town is exactly 120 miles along one continuous route.
The gas station is exactly on the route at mile 60.
The vehicle must have enough fuel for the entire next 10-mile movement before that movement begins.
There are no fuel leaks, mechanical failures, detours, road closures, fuel prices, payment constraints, or other vehicles.
The driver knows the route, the station location, the vehicle tank capacity, and the assumed fuel economy.
The delivery is successful only when the vehicle reaches the town; merely arriving near the town does not count.
processes_each_tick: If the vehicle is operational and has enough fuel for the next 10 miles, the vehicle and driver advance 10 miles toward the town.
Each 10-mile movement reduces vehicle fuel by 0.4 gallons.
Road distance remaining decreases by the vehicle's movement distance.
If the vehicle reaches the gas station and the driver refuels, vehicle fuel increases by the purchased amount and gas-station fuel stock decreases by the same amount.
Fuel cannot exceed the vehicle tank capacity or the gas station's available fuel stock.

If the vehicle lacks enough fuel to complete the next 10-mile movement, it stops, its operational status becomes failed, and the delivery cannot be completed unless refueling is possible at its current location.
When the vehicle reaches mile 120 while operational, the town's delivery_received state becomes true and the trip ends.
If the vehicle reaches or passes the gas station's position, the gas station is available for refueling only at mile 60.
odd.purpose: Determine whether the delivery driver can reach the town 120 miles away with a quarter tank, with or without refueling at the gas station at mile 60.

can_observe: Current fuel level and approximate fraction of tank remaining.
The gas station at mile 60 when approaching or reaching it.
Whether the gas station is open and has fuel available when the driver is there.
cannot_observe: Future fuel consumption deviations from the assumed rate.
Any gas station fuel stock beyond what is observable at the station.
Whether the vehicle will fail before the next movement except through the current fuel state and assumed consumption rate.

inflows: Fuel purchased and transferred from the gas station into the vehicle.

outflows: Fuel purchased by the driver and transferred to the vehicle.

inflows: Vehicle movement of 10 miles per completed driving tick.
Vehicle reaching the town at mile 120 while operational.

odd.time_step: 1 tick = 10 miles of driving; 12 ticks represent the full 120-mile trip, and the gas station is reached after 6 ticks.
